entries.title: White Sox rookie Noah Schultz shines in second start, Murakami homers again in win
entries.summary: <p>WEST SACRAMENTO, Calif. — The lowly <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a> were due for a bang-up afternoon, and they got one Sunday against the Athletics.</p><p>There was Japanese phenom Munetaka Murakami admiring his towering home run for a third straight game. There were Colson Montgomery and Miguel Vargas tagging their own impressive blasts, plus Chase Meidroth scratching out two hits.</p><p>Nevermind a few late bullpen hiccups, because most importantly, there was left-hander Noah Schultz dealing through five strong innings in the second start of his career — and letting his 97-mph sinker answer any lingering questions about <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/14/noah-schultz-white-sox-mlb-debut" target="_blank" ><u>his shaky Chicago debut</u></a> last week.</p><p>The Aurora native gave up a solo home run, a walk and nothing else while striking out six over five innings against a powerful Athletics lineup en route to a 7-4 win. He threw 82 pitches, identical to his first outing last Tuesday at Rate Field that was spoiled by a three-run first inning including a two-run throwing error from the 6-10 Schultz.</p><p>Schultz was charged with an error in West Sacramento, too, after he couldn’t handle Murakami’s toss while covering first on a grounder. But there wasn’t any hint of jitters from the Oswego East product who acknowledged he had to shake them off the first time he took the mound.</p><p>Schultz, who served up the first home run of his career to A’s third baseman Darell Hernaiz, had the benefit of healthy run support from an offense that has found its footing on the West Coast.</p><p>Catcher Edgar Quero knocked a sacrifice fly in the first inning, and the Sox continued feasting on A’s starter Jeffrey Springs in the second with a solo homer from Derek Hill and Vargas’ two-run blast.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Munetaka Murakami has hit 8 home runs this season.<br><br>This is the SECOND time he's homered in 3 straight games! <a href="https://t.co/KsSpNTOxOU">https://t.co/KsSpNTOxOU</a> <a href="https://t.co/rEz6I0pRH4">pic.twitter.com/rEz6I0pRH4</a></p>— MLB (@MLB) <a href="https://twitter.com/MLB/status/2045977413570470303?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">April 19, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.twitter.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Sox then staked Schultz to a 7-1 lead in the fifth inning with Murakami’s latest eye-popping blast, a two-run shot sent sailing at 114 mph off the bat and 415 deep past the outfield lawn at Sutter Health Park. It marked his eighth U.S. homer and the second three-game homer streak of his budding career, following his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/01/munetaka-murakami-chicago-white-sox-debut" target="_blank" ><u>torrid opening weekend</u></a> with the Sox.</p><p>Montgomery followed up with his own 419-foot shot to straightaway center field for his fifth homer of the season and second in as many days.</p><p>But after watching a five-run lead evaporate on Saturday, Sox relievers let the Athletics chip away in the seventh inning. The A’s tagged Grant Taylor for two runs in the seventh inning on a double from second baseman Zack Gelof, then plated another on a wild pitch from Jordan Leasure.</p><p>Reliever Bryan Hudson escaped the eighth after giving up a double, and closer <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/17/white-sox-seranthony-dominguez-anthony-kay-athletics?99" target="_blank" ><u>Seranthony Dominguez</u></a> worked around a walk and a hit batter to seal the win. </p>
entries.author: Mitchell Armentrout

entries.title: Kamala Harris says in Chicago that Trump ‘has made America weaker’
entries.summary: <p>During an appearance Sunday in Chicago, former Vice President Kamala Harris said President Trump’s war on Iran has “made America weaker.”</p><p>“He is the first president, Republican or Democrat since World War II, to not concern himself [with] the importance of America's alliances, our friendships and America's responsibility to uphold standards such as sovereignty and territorial integrity,” Harris told a crowd at the Power Rising Summit, a convening of Black women harnessing their collective wisdom to create an actionable agenda.</p><p>The conversation happened at the Soul Sunday Brunch on the final day of the three-day event at the downtown Hilton Chicago. She was interviewed by summit founder Leah Daughtry, CEO of the 2008 Democratic National Convention Committee.</p><p>Harris said the country’s involvement in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nation-world/2026/03/01/chicagoans-iran-middle-east-ties-worry-united-states-israel-continue-bombing" target="_blank" ><u>war in Iran</u></a>, a “war the American people don’t want,” is a result of Trump “just getting persuaded by” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netenayhu.</p><p>She said Trump’s actions have “caused us to become more unreliable and to lose our influence to then be able — imperfect, though, we certainly are flawed — to talk about matters of human rights around the world.”</p><p>The Biden-Harris administration was not free of criticism regarding human rights. In March, <a class="Link" href="https://www.axios.com/2026/02/22/dnc-2024-autopsy-harris-gaza" target="_blank" ><u>Axios</u></a> reported that a hidden DNC report found that the Biden administration’s position on the war in Gaza cost Harris the 2024 election.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez listens to Harris speak during the “Power Rising" summit." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/82639b6/2147483647/strip/true/crop/7376x4140+0+390/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F25%2Fc6%2Fd3fb6cc749a39292a56db71601c4%2Fharris-260420-007.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/257b197/2147483647/strip/true/crop/7376x4140+0+390/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F25%2Fc6%2Fd3fb6cc749a39292a56db71601c4%2Fharris-260420-007.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/82639b6/2147483647/strip/true/crop/7376x4140+0+390/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F25%2Fc6%2Fd3fb6cc749a39292a56db71601c4%2Fharris-260420-007.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez listens to Harris speak during the “Power Rising” summit.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Candace Dane Chambers/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Looking ahead to this November’s midterm elections, Harris said “it’s gonna be so difficult” for the Democrats to win, but that the path includes “a vision for affordable child care, affordable health care, affordable housing and … a vision that is about actually getting this stuff done.”</p><p>Harris criticized leaders, including Democrats, who are in office and "preserving their title at the expense of actually getting anything done.</p><p>“And then when you try to look at what they've actually done to move the needle, you're left wanting,” she said. “And so part of the work has to be accountability.”</p><p>In 2028 and beyond, Harris said she believes that “America is, can be and will be ready for a woman to be president of the United States.” Harris <a class="Link" href="https://www.cnn.com/2026/04/10/politics/kamala-harris-2028-presidential-election" target="_blank" ><u>said earlier this month</u></a> that she’s “thinking about” another run. If elected, she would become the first woman to hold the office, adding to a list of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2020/8/11/21363819/biden-picks-kamala-harris-for-running-mate" target="_blank" ><u>firsts</u></a> throughout her career: The first Black person and first woman to be elected as California’s Attorney General, and the first woman and first Black person to be Vice President of the United States.</p><p>"There are still certain myths about what a woman can and cannot do in spite of what she actually does,” Harris said. “My mother sat me down to say that, for me to get ready for what it would mean to run, and she followed that up by saying it's a myth.”<br></p>
